column1: # Delivery styles: one row per style a task is given (direct-PR, local). Columns: mode, the line, what it adds in delivering, how it joins main, publishes (yes when the line goes to a forge as a pull request), review (yes when the pipeline review and its intent overlay run), trunk (yes when the lane lands as one commit on the local trunk).

# An alias row is an old mode word read as a style: alias, the old word, the style it reads as, the trunk fact the old word carried and its rule1, so an old record is read as before. yolo stays the merge switch: with it off a `local` lane waits for a word, with it on it lands by itself. An alias may carry a sixth field, the review fact the old word carried, so a record that says no-mistakes keeps its head accepted when a pipeline pushed it.
# A style changes only the stage delivering. No column names a prover: done-done proves the commit in every mode.
# rule1 (column 9) is the first ship rule; {target} and {branch} are filled by the brief. Columns are read by name through `jg-delivery-style.sh --field`, which uses the `columns` row.
